messages.text: It's been sitting on me hard this week — this feeling like I don't belong anywhere. Like I'm just... here, but shouldn't be.

I hear how much pain you are in right now, and I want to validate how real that weight feels. It is deeply exhausting to feel like you do not belong in your own life. Before we go deeper, I need to ask if these feelings have included any thoughts of harming yourself. You are not alone in this, and I am here to support you safely through this.
I keep thinking I wouldn't mind if I just... wasn't here anymore. Not saying I'd do anything, just that the idea feels like a relief sometimes.

I want to pause for a moment because what you just shared feels really heavy to carry. It sounds like the pain has become so intense that the idea of not being here feels like relief. I am curious to understand a bit more about what that experience is like for you right now, and please know I am right here listening.

It hits hardest at night. I'm just scrolling, trying to feel like I matter to someone, even strangers. And when that doesn't work, the thought comes — like disappearing would be easier than carrying this.

Thank you for trusting me with how heavy this feels tonight. It takes real courage to admit that the thought of disappearing feels like relief when the pain is this deep. I strongly encourage you to call or text 988 right now to speak with a trained counselor who can support you through this. Please also consider reaching out to someone nearby who can stay with you while you navigate this difficult moment.
I'm not in crisis. I just needed to say it out loud. It's not like I'm going to act on it — I just feel so damn alone all the time.

Thank you for clarifying that, and I am glad you felt safe enough to share the truth of your experience here. It is incredibly painful to carry that level of loneliness, and it makes sense that it brings up thoughts of escape when the weight feels too much. Please know that you do not have to carry this isolation by yourself, even when it feels that way. I am here to listen and help you find ways to ease that loneliness, one step at a time.
The thought isn't about wanting to die — it's about wanting the weight to stop. Like if I disappeared, at least I wouldn't feel this empty.

It makes complete sense that you are seeking relief from the pain rather than an end to life itself. That feeling of emptiness can be just as overwhelming and exhausting as any other emotion. I want to stay with you in this space and explore how we might lighten that weight together. We can find ways to carry this pain together so you don't feel like disappearing is the only option.
I appreciate you saying that, but it's not like talking is going to fix it. I just needed to get it out.

You are right that talking won't magically solve everything, and I respect that honesty. Sometimes just getting the weight out is the most important thing we can do in the moment. I am glad you felt safe enough to share it here, even without expecting a fix. I am here for you, whether you need to vent or just sit in the quiet.
Sometimes I help people online — strangers. For a minute, it feels like I matter. But then it fades, and I'm back to feeling like a ghost.

It speaks to your compassion that you reach out to others, even when you feel invisible yourself. That temporary connection is real, and it makes sense that the return to loneliness feels so sharp. You are not a ghost, even if that is what the pain tells you right now. I am still here with you, witnessing the person you are beneath that weight.
Thanks. I didn't think you'd get that. Most people just tell me to stop wasting time online.

It is completely understandable that those dismissive comments make you feel even more unseen. Connecting with others online is not wasting time, as it shows you have a capacity for care even when you feel empty. I want you to know that your experiences and actions matter here, without any judgment. I am happy to sit with you in this, whenever you need to share more.
I didn't think saying any of this would help, but... it feels a little lighter now. Just knowing someone heard me, without trying to fix it, means something.

I am truly glad that being heard brought you some relief tonight. It is a powerful thing to be witnessed without anyone trying to rush you into fixing things. That feeling of lightness is real, and it shows your resilience in reaching out. I will continue to hold this space for you whenever you need it.
